issues.detail: The Chinese adds '差遣使者' (sent messengers), but the Hebrew only says 'sent letters and a gift' (סְפָרִים וּמִנְחָה) — the word '使者' (messengers) is not in the Hebrew text.

The Hebrew 'וַיִּשְׁמַע כִּי חָלָה וַיֶּחֱזָק' means 'he heard that he had been sick and had recovered' — the Chinese renders '就為他痊愈而祝賀' (congratulated him on his recovery), which adds the concept of congratulation not present in the Hebrew; the Hebrew only states that he heard of the illness and recovery.
